title: Cozy Cottage Coloring Book for Adults
subtitle: 50 Bold and Easy Scenes of Gardens, Kitchens and Reading Nooks
author: Clara Whitcombe
blurb: 50 cozy cottage, garden and kitchen scenes ready to be colored.
Bold, clean lines and open shapes that are easy to see and relaxing to color.
Single-sided pages with a blank page behind each picture.
The inside pages are black and white. The colors on the cover are just an example!
description:
Step into a world of cozy cottages, blooming gardens and warm kitchens with 50 bold and easy coloring pages for adults. Each single-sided picture is drawn with clean, confident lines and open shapes: a thatched cottage and its garden gate, a window seat with a sleeping cat, a tea table with scones, a bookshelf full of treasures, beehives among the lavender, a rabbit in the vegetable patch and much more.

What's inside
• 50 one-sided coloring pages, with a blank page behind each picture
• Cottages, gardens, kitchens, reading nooks and cozy animals
• Bold, clean outlines with clearly separated areas: no tiny fiddly details
• A "This book belongs to" page and a color test page
• Large 8.5 x 11 inch pages

A pleasant hobby for quiet evenings and an easy gift for anyone who loves gardens, tea and books. Works well with colored pencils, gel pens and markers (slip a sheet of scrap paper behind the page when you use markers).

The inside pages are printed in black and white, ready for you to color. The colors on the cover are just an example.

The illustrations in this book were generated with AI image tools and were selected and arranged by the publisher, Little Fox Paper Co.

notes: **Rebuilt 2026-11-14.** The first version (40 finely detailed scenes) printed crackly: fine textures broke into marks too small to color. All pages were regenerated in a bold, clean style and the book grew to 50 pictures, the usual size for this kind of book.

**Keywords 5 and 6** describe the bold lines and single-sided pages; the book is not printed in a special large-print format and uses normal KDP paper, so markers can show through (hence the blank backs). Drop either keyword if you find it too strong.
**Cover style.** The cover uses the same playful family as the kids' books because that is the current project rule; an adult-style cover is recommended (see TODO).
